title: Tanzanian Mixed Vegetables
community: Urban Tanzania — the restaurant and hotel vegetable side
author: Chef Jabir
desc: Tanzanian Mboga Mchanganyiko — a colourful medley of seasonal Tanzanian vegetables blanched and sautéed with garlic and herbs. The restaurant and hotel vegetable side that showcases Tanzania's excellent highland vegetable production.
longDesc: Tanzania's central highlands — particularly around Arusha, Kilimanjaro, and the Southern Highlands — produce excellent vegetables. The mixed vegetable preparation at Tanzanian restaurants takes these quality ingredients and treats them correctly: blanched briefly to preserve colour, finished in garlic butter.
steps: Blanch each vegetable separately in heavily salted boiling water: carrots 3 min, beans and broccoli 2 min, courgette and corn 1 min.
Immediately transfer each to ice water. Drain well.
Heat butter or oil in a wide pan over medium-high.
Add garlic. Cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add all blanched vegetables. Toss to coat.
Add lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
chefTips: The ice bath is what keeps the vegetables brilliantly coloured.
Each vegetable needs different blanching times — work in batches.
Serve immediately after the final toss — vegetables lose colour and crispness quickly.
commonMistakes: No ice bath — dull, overcooked colours.
Single blanching time for all vegetables.
cookingScience: See KEN278 for the full science of blanching and ice bath vegetable preservation.
sustainabilityTips: Tanzania's highland vegetables have very short supply chains to urban centres.
storage: Blanched vegetables keep 2 days. Reheat in pan.
culturalNote: Mixed vegetables at a Tanzanian restaurant or hotel signal a kitchen that cares about every part of the meal — the green vegetables served alongside the pilau or grilled fish are as important as the main event.
